fieldissues.issue: The title does not name Trump, the 2020 protests, or the Insurrection Act.
“Massive violation” describes a threat as an established legal violation, and “authoritarian escalation” is editorial framing.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Threatens to Invoke Insurrection Act During 2020 Protests
proposedchanges.description_medium: Replace the legal conclusion and editorial label with a concise account of Trump’s June 1 threat to deploy federal troops if states did not act and his demand that governors dominate the streets.

evidencebasis: The supplied transcript records Trump’s remarks to governors and his conditional threat to deploy the military. The merged record retains the transcript, contemporaneous report, and Washington Post URLs.
notes: Keep the threat distinct from a formal invocation or completed deployment.

fieldissues.issue: The title does not identify Trump or the 2020 election.
“Premeditated lie” and “launched his campaign to subvert” assign intent and later consequences beyond the election-night transcript.
The long refers to the “available record,” “this entry,” and the “preserved” transcript, and repeats that later efforts are outside its scope.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Declares Victory While the 2020 Vote Count Continues
proposedchanges.description_medium: State that Trump claimed victory and called the ongoing count “a major fraud” while ballots were still being counted. Remove the claims about premeditation and later subversion.
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentences beginning “The available record directly supports,” “Nor does this entry,” and “The statement is preserved.” Keep the quoted remarks, timing, and status of the count without inferring intent.

evidencebasis: The Roll Call/Factbase transcript records Trump’s victory and fraud statements while counting continued. The current long repeatedly discusses the transcript and its limits instead of the event.
notes: Attribute the quote and do not treat the speech alone as proof of the scope or coordination of later efforts.

fieldissues.issue: “Flees” can suggest Pence left voluntarily, while the committee report describes a Secret Service evacuation.
The medium says agents feared for their lives and nearly forced Pence from the complex, details not identified in the supplied report note.
The long refers to the supplied account and source note, then says the entry makes no additional claims; this is editorial commentary.
The packet supplies the January 6 Committee report but no source for the agents’ fear or the claimed near-forced removal.

proposedchanges.title: Secret Service Evacuates Vice President Pence From the Senate Floor
proposedchanges.description_medium: Use the committee report’s documented evacuation and movement to a secure location. Add an exact source before retaining the claims about agents’ fear or forceful removal.
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentences beginning “The supplied account says,” “The committee report supports,” “The episode is part,” and “The cited report documents.” Add exact support for any retained detail about agents’ decisions or the full movement sequence.
proposedchanges.source_urls: Retain the January 6 Committee report and add an exact source for the agents’ fear and alleged near-forced removal if those claims remain.

evidencebasis: The committee support note documents Pence’s evacuation from the Senate floor, movement to a secure location, and the chant. It does not mention the agents’ fear or forceful removal.
notes: Keep the evacuation and chant attributed to the report and distinguish them from unsupported detail.

fieldissues.issue: The title omits that the records concerned the end-of-term transfer from Trump’s presidency.
The medium explains that the link is unrelated instead of presenting the event to a reader.
The long is null, so the record lacks a detailed explanation.
The only link is a National Archives response to the January 6 attack and does not document the missing-records timeline or Mar-a-Lago requests.

proposedchanges.title: National Archives Seeks Presidential Records Missing From Trump’s Transfer
proposedchanges.description_medium: Remove the sentence explaining what the linked source fails to document. Keep the stated discovery and requests for return attributed until an event-specific source is supplied.
proposedchanges.description_long: Add a reader-facing account only after a relevant National Archives statement, court filing, or reporting source verifies which records were missing, when NARA identified the issue, and what happened after its requests.
proposedchanges.source_urls: Replace the unrelated January 6 press release with exact sources for the records-recovery timeline and requests.

evidencebasis: The packet’s NARA link is titled “U.S. Archivist Responds to Capitol Riots.” It does not match the described records-recovery event; no long description is present in the merged record.
notes: Do not infer document contents, classification, intent, or legal outcome without a matching source.

fieldissues.issue: “Most of the money” overstates the packet’s finding that much of the money went elsewhere, including Save America PAC.
The long repeatedly refers to the supplied source note, the entry, and what the information does not specify, rather than explaining the committee’s finding in a natural account.

proposedchanges.description_medium: Replace “Most of the money was funneled” with “Much of the money went to Trump’s Save America PAC and other political uses rather than the election litigation suggested by the fundraising pitch.”
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the phrases “according to the January 6 Committee’s final report” only where repeated, and remove sentences beginning “The entry describes,” “The final report is,” and “The exact allocation.” State the committee’s finding once, attribute it, and avoid implying that no election litigation occurred.

evidencebasis: The supplied House Select Committee note says Trump and the RNC raised more than $250 million with the nonexistent fund pitch and that much of the money went elsewhere. The merged description retains the official report URL.
notes: Keep “much” rather than “most” unless the source quantifies a majority, and distinguish fundraising claims from the existence of separate litigation.
